statements.text: The task model carries a nullable `deletedAt` timestamp, serialized in JSON as `deletedAt`: an ISO-8601 string when set, `null` while the task is active.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` on an active task sets `deletedAt` to the current time and returns 204 No Content; the task is retained in the store, not permanently removed.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` for an unknown id returns 404 Not Found.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` for an already soft-deleted task returns 404 Not Found and leaves the existing `deletedAt` unchanged.
`GET /tasks` returns only active (not soft-deleted) tasks by default.
`GET /tasks?includeDeleted=true` returns all tasks, including soft-deleted ones (non-null `deletedAt`).
`GET /tasks/{id}` returns 404 Not Found for a soft-deleted task and 200 OK for an active one.
The four seeded tasks are active (`deletedAt` = null) after startup — existing rows keep working with no migration step.
The five pre-existing integration tests still pass and the other CRUD endpoints (POST, PUT, validation) keep their current behaviour.

Visibility filtering stays at the endpoint/query boundary: `TaskStore.All()` / `Get()` keep their shapes, only the `Remove` mutator becomes `SoftDelete`; `Domain/**` references no ASP.NET type (R-004) and `TaskState` naming is unchanged (R-005).
